LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD contains only standard, top-level variable assignments in its global scope: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `optdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `options`, `source_*` arrays, and `sha256sums_*` arrays. There are no command substitutions (`$()`), no top-level function calls, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, and no base64 decoding or obfuscated payloads anywhere that would execute while the file is sourced.

The `source_x86_64` and `source_aarch64` arrays reference the project's own declared upstream GitHub releases (`github.com/bhimio1/CreativeCraft/releases`) via variable interpolation, but this is a static assignment — no network request occurs during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` (downloads and verification happen in later stages, and SKIP/nonexistent checksums are explicitly out of scope for this gate). The `package()` function is merely defined, not invoked, so its contents cannot execute during this command.

Nothing in the global scope downloads, executes, or exfiltrates anything. This is an ordinary binary PKGBUILD whose only top-level behavior is declaring metadata and checksums, which is entirely consistent with standard packaging practice.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No executable or network code in global scope; only metadata assignments.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No executable or network code in global scope; only metadata assignments.

Both source URLs point to the package's declared upstream, which is standard practice for -bin packages. Both sources include valid SHA256 checksums (not SKIP), so build-time integrity verification is enforced. Dependencies are standard Linux/X11 libraries with no suspicious extras. No exfiltration, no reverse shells, no remote code execution, and no unexpected file operations are present.
